headline: Zvezda's home scoring meets Copenhagen's 3-0 start
summary: Crvena Zvezda have scored 15 goals in their last five games, and that scoring is why the market still favours them after a 3-2 defeat at Lugano, where a late penalty decided it. Copenhagen opened with a 3-0 home win over Braga. Across 10 bookmakers, with the margin removed, Zvezda are 42.0% to win and Copenhagen 31.9% — a close game. The handicap, a head start in goals, has the home side only a quarter of a goal better, and over 2.75 goals carries a 50.9% chance.
read: Crvena Zvezda are narrow home favourites at 42.0% despite losing 3-2 at Lugano, because their home form is scoring for fun — 15 goals in five games, including 5-1 on Sunday. Copenhagen arrive second in the table after a 3-0 win over Braga, and the market expects an open game: the total line is 2.75 with over at 50.9% and both teams to score at 60.2%.

facts.fact: Crvena Zvezda are the market's favourites at 42.0% to win in Belgrade.
facts.meaning: They are rated about a quarter of a goal better than Copenhagen on the handicap (-0.25) — a home win is favoured, but the tie is close to even.

facts.fact: Crvena Zvezda lost their Conference League opener 3-2 at Lugano, with a late penalty deciding it.
facts.meaning: They sit 24th of 36 with no points, so the home game already carries knockout-round weight.

facts.fact: Copenhagen opened their campaign with a 3-0 home win over Braga.
facts.meaning: They arrive second in the 36-team table with a +3 goal difference and a clean sheet.

facts.fact: Crvena Zvezda beat Mladost Lucani 5-1 on Sunday with 6.02 xG.
facts.meaning: Their chance creation at home is at a level Copenhagen's back line has not met in the Danish league.

facts.fact: Copenhagen drew 1-1 at home with Aarhus on Sunday despite 2.01 xG.
facts.meaning: Two points dropped at Parken, and Midtjylland are now level on points with them at the top of the Superliga.

facts.fact: The market's total-goals line is 2.75, with over priced at 50.9%.
facts.meaning: The market expects a game around the three-goal mark — a 2-1 or 2-2 shape rather than a grind.

facts.fact: Both teams to score is priced at 60.2%.
facts.meaning: Both sides finding the net is more likely than not; a clean sheet either way is the minority view.

facts.fact: Their only previous meetings, in 2019 Champions League qualifying, both finished level — 1-1 in Belgrade and 2-2 in Copenhagen — before a penalty shootout.
facts.meaning: Recent history between these clubs is tight and level, which fits a match the market has at 42% / 26% / 32%.

sources.fact: Crvena zvezda lost 3-2 away at Lugano in their Conference League opener, with a late penalty deciding it.
Crvena zvezda host Copenhagen at the Rajko Mitić stadium on Thursday 22 October in the second round of the Conference League, still chasing their first points of the campaign.
Serbian outlet Sportska centrala reports that Crvena zvezda will line up slightly changed from the Lugano defeat, though no major changes are expected.
Serbian outlet Novosti reports that Ivanić and Katić have returned ahead of the Copenhagen match.
Marko Marin, now the club's technical director, recalled the 2019 penalty shootout against the Danes ahead of this fixture.
Midtjylland's derby win over Viborg drew them level on points with Copenhagen at the top of the Danish Superliga.
Parken Sport and Entertainment is exploring a full or partial sale of FC Copenhagen as part of a strategic review of its football business, Inside World Football reports.
Thapelo Maseko featured for Copenhagen in their Conference League match against Braga on 15 October.

key_points: Market sees close to three goals
